title: [Flight] Avoid main-thread stalls from large debug strings
message: The replay expectation assumes the placeholder replaces only the second argument to `console.log`, but the implementation change is in `renderDebugModel` and may affect how the entire debug value is encoded/decoded. Can you confirm that replay still preserves the original argument count and ordering for multi-arg console calls, especially if one argument is omitted while others are retained? If not, this test could pass while masking a client-side formatting regression.
reason: The omission only swaps the long string for a placeholder via per-value serialization (serializeDebugLargeTextString/outlineDebugModel), encoding each console arg independently, so argument count and ordering are preserved as the test asserts (arg[0]='large string:', arg[1]=placeholder); the finding's concern about losing args is unfounded and the test is a legitimate, well-targeted addition.

title: [19.0.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: `field` events are now queued onto the current `tail` file whenever any file is in flight. If payload order is `file A -> file B -> field for A`, that field will be attached to B instead of A, so the decoded FormData can still come out of order or lose the original grouping when multiple files are buffered concurrently. Consider tracking the file that was current when the field arrived, rather than always using the latest tail.
reason: Multipart payloads are linear and busboy processes parts sequentially, so a field emitted after file B's 'file' event genuinely follows B in payload order; queuing it on the tail file correctly preserves FormData insertion order, contradicting the finding's premise that the field could belong before B.

title: [19.0.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: `bodyFinished` is only set from Busboy's `finish` event. If a file stream emits `error` or `busboyStream.destroy(error)` aborts parsing before `finish`, `close(response)` is never called from this path and the reply promise can hang unless the error path closes it elsewhere. Please verify the error handler always resolves or rejects the pending reply.
reason: The busboyStream.on('error') handler (and destroy(error) which emits 'error') calls reportGlobalError(response, err), and file stream 'error' is wired to busboyStream.destroy(error), so the error path does settle the reply rather than hang; the finding's "unless the error path closes it elsewhere" caveat is in fact satisfied.

title: [19.1.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: `busboyStream.on('finish')` assumes every file has already fired `'end'`, but if a file stream is paused/backpressured or an error path delays completion, `flush()` can return early and this reports a global error instead of closing cleanly. Could this close be deferred until all pending files are drained rather than treating the invariant as fatal?
reason: Busboy's API defers 'finish' until every consumed file stream's 'end' fires (and the 'data' handler consumes each stream), so flush() always closes cleanly under backpressure; the reportGlobalError is a documented defensive invariant guard, not a misfire on normal completion.

title: [19.1.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: Fields are queued only while `tail !== null`, but once the head file completes and `flush()` advances, a text field arriving before the next file's `'file'` event will resolve immediately even though a later file may already be part of the same multipart ordering. That can reintroduce the ordering bug this patch is trying to fix. Consider tracking whether any pending file is still unflushed rather than just whether `tail` exists.
reason: In flush() (lines 254-281), `tail` is set to null only after the while loop fully drains all pending files; if a later file is still incomplete the loop returns early at the `!current.complete` check (line 257-260) without nulling `tail`, so a field arriving while any file is still in flight is still queued, and `tail===null` truly means no file is pending—making immediate field resolution correct rather than a reintroduced ordering bug.

title: [19.1.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: These tests validate the no-drop behavior for a very specific interleaving, but do not cover the case where a text field arrives after one file completes and before the next file event begins. Was that timing considered when changing from a global queue to per-file queues?
reason: The decoder uses a per-file linked list where a field arriving after a file completes (tail set to null only in flush) resolves immediately or queues on the tail, and the "field after one file completes and before the next file" case is functionally identical to cases already covered; the finding is a speculative coverage question, not a worth-posting bug.

title: [19.2.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: `finish` now relies on every pending file eventually calling `end`, but if a file stream emits an error after `finish` has been observed, `closed` stays false and the code reports a synthetic 'incomplete file part' error in addition to the underlying stream error. Could this double-report or mask the real failure path? Consider guarding `finish` handling after any busboy/file error or centralizing terminal-state handling.
reason: The 'error' handler calls busboyStream.destroy(error), which makes the stream emit 'close'/'error' rather than 'finish', so the described "error after finish observed" sequence can't occur; the synthetic 'incomplete file part' error is a defensive invariant guard (per the code's documented busboy ordering), not a realistic double-report path.

title: [19.2.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: Queued text fields are only flushed when the head file completes. If busboy ever emits a `field` after a later file has already completed but before the earlier head file ends, that field is attached to the tail file and delayed until the head finishes. That preserves payload order, but it also means a failure in the head file can now drop unrelated later fields that were already fully parsed. Please verify this is intended; otherwise fields may be lost on partial file failures.
reason: On a head-file failure, flush calls busboyStream.destroy(error) which triggers the 'error' handler → reportGlobalError, failing the entire reply as a unit, so there is no partial-success path where queued fields are silently "lost" to the consumer.

title: [19.0.x] Enable CI
message: `ServerReferenceId` was changed from an opaque type to a plain string type. Was this intentional for this fork? Making it a regular `string` removes the nominal distinction that prevents accidentally passing arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected, which can hide bugs in the Flight client/server protocol. If the runtime truly only ever treats it as a string, consider keeping an opaque wrapper on the public boundary and only unwrapping internally.
reason: The canonical bundler configs (ReactFlightClientConfigBundlerWebpack.js:45 and ReactFlightClientConfigBundlerESM.js:21) both define `ServerReferenceId` as a plain non-opaque `string`, so the markup fork change just aligns the type with the rest of the codebase; no nominal protection exists elsewhere to be "lost."

title: [19.1.x] Enable CI
message: This entry point now only exports `unstable_prerenderToNodeStream`, dropping the previously public `prerender` and `prerenderToNodeStream` symbols. Any existing Node consumers importing those names will start failing at runtime with `undefined` exports. If the API is meant to stay backward compatible, re-export the old names as aliases or keep the previous exports in addition to the unstable one.
reason: The source entry point react-flight-dom-server.node.js only exports prerenderToNodeStream as unstable_prerenderToNodeStream (no `prerender` export and no stable name), so the npm wrapper change merely aligns with the actual unstable-prefixed API rather than dropping a backward-compatible public export.

title: [19.1.x] Enable CI
message: `ServerReferenceId` changed from an opaque type to a plain `string`. That removes Flow's nominal boundary and makes it easier to accidentally pass arbitrary strings where a server reference ID is expected. Was the opacity intentionally dropped for this fork, or should this stay opaque to preserve type-safety across the client/server boundary?
reason: The canonical webpack fork already declares `export type ServerReferenceId = string;` non-opaque, and in this markup fork server references are never resolved (all related functions throw), so dropping `opaque` is a harmless consistency alignment, not a type-safety regression.

title: ♻️ Do not accept underscore headers when using `convert_underscores=True` (the default)
message: `processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))` is now applied for every parameter type handled by `request_params_to_args`, not just headers. If this helper is reused for query/cookie params, or if a field’s validation alias differs from the received key shape, this can incorrectly suppress 'extra' detection for unrelated inputs. Consider restricting this extra processed-key entry to header parameters only, or gating it on `convert_underscores` being active.
reason: Line 832 adds `get_validation_alias(field)`, which for non-header params equals the value already added by `alias or get_validation_alias(field)` on line 828 (since `alias` is None unless `received_params` is `Headers` with convert_underscores), so the new line is a no-op set insertion for query/cookie params and only adds the underscore form for headers where suppressing it is intended.

title: 📝 Add docs references to central contributing docs
message: `translations.md` is now treated as one of the core docs. If this file does not exist under `docs/` (or is generated later than the other docs), `scripts/docs.py` may fail or start reporting a missing-docs error. Could you confirm the file is present and intended to be part of the required set?
reason: The edited tuple is `non_translated_sections`, used only by `is_non_translated_path` as a startswith filter to skip missing-translation banners (lines 185-187, 244); it is not a required-docs set, so a missing `translations.md` causes no failure or missing-docs error.

title: 🔧 Migrate docs from MkDocs to Zensical
message: `is_non_translated_path()` now checks `path.as_posix().startswith(section)`, but `non_translated_sections` contains `reference{os.sep}`. On POSIX this yields `reference/`, which is fine, but on Windows `as_posix()` always uses `/` while `section` may contain `\`, so untranslated reference pages will be treated as translatable. Consider normalizing both sides to POSIX-style separators before comparing.
reason: Confirmed at lines 41-42 and 184-186: non_translated_sections uses `reference{os.sep}` while is_non_translated_path compares against `path.as_posix()`, so on Windows `reference\` never matches `reference/`, causing reference pages to be incorrectly treated as translatable—a genuine separator-mismatch bug introduced by this diff.

title: 🔧 Migrate docs from MkDocs to Zensical
message: The new untranslated-page check only skips files under `reference/` and a few specific markdown files. The old hook also preserved other non-translated assets via MkDocs' file resolution. Because the staging step now copies the English tree and only overlays translated markdown, any untranslated non-markdown assets under language-specific docs will silently fall back to English without the previous explicit handling. If that is intentional, fine; otherwise it may break localized asset paths.
reason: Staging copies the entire English source tree (line 219) so all non-markdown assets are present, and translation dirs like docs/es/docs contain only .md files, so the English fallback for assets matches the prior INHERIT behavior—no broken localized asset paths exist.

title: 🔧 Migrate docs from MkDocs to Zensical
message: `live()` no longer accepts a language argument and always serves `en/docs`. This changes the behavior from previewing translated docs to English-only preview, which makes it impossible to verify non-English output locally via the documented command. If translated preview is still needed, consider keeping the `lang` parameter and pointing Zensical at the selected language stage.
reason: The `live()` simplification to English-only is an intentional part of the mkdocs→Zensical migration with a matching updated docstring, and translated previews remain available via the `serve` command, so the finding merely second-guesses a deliberate design choice rather than identifying a bug.

title: Remove unnecessary null check
message: `getProperties().getLettuce()` is dereferenced unconditionally here, but `RedisProperties#getLettuce()` is not proven non-null by the diff. If a user has no `spring.redis.lettuce.*` configuration, this will now throw a `NullPointerException` during bean creation. Please keep the null guard or ensure the property is initialized defensively.
reason: RedisProperties initializes `private final Lettuce lettuce = new Lettuce()` (line 99), so `getLettuce()` can never be null and the removed null guard was redundant.

title: Layer written outside the output location of '//' exception is thrown when using extract layers in root directory
message: `outputRoot.relativize(layerDirectory)` can produce an empty path component when `layerDirectory` is created under a temp dir on a filesystem with a different root representation, which would make `layerName` empty or unexpected. Since the test later uses this value as both the iterator result and the expected layer name, it may not actually validate the intended root-destination case reliably. Consider hardcoding a simple relative layer name (for example, `dependencies`) and keeping only `outputRoot` as the destination under test.
reason: Since layerDirectory is an absolute normalized path with at least "root-output/dependencies" components, relativizing it against its own getRoot() always yields a non-empty multi-segment path; the empty-component concern is speculative and the suggested "fix" would make the test write to the actual filesystem root, defeating the test's safe construction.

title: Use new Maven Resolver API for ModifiedClassPathClassLoader
message: `RepositorySystemSupplier` may return a `RepositorySystem` implementation that does not expose `shutdown()`. If so, this call will fail at runtime or silently be ineffective depending on the API version. Could you confirm the supplier’s returned type and whether `shutdown()` is guaranteed here? If not, the safe pattern is to guard this call or avoid assuming lifecycle management on the `RepositorySystem` interface.
reason: The build.gradle uses maven-resolver-supplier (Resolver 1.9+) where RepositorySystem.shutdown() is a guaranteed interface method, so the call compiles against the interface and is always available, contradicting the finding's concern.

title: Use new Maven Resolver API for ModifiedClassPathClassLoader
message: Creating a new `RepositorySystem` for every `resolveCoordinates` call may be expensive, since this code can run repeatedly while scanning annotations. If this method is called often, consider caching/reusing the resolver instance instead of constructing and tearing it down each time.
reason: resolveCoordinates runs only for the rare @ClassPathOverrides test annotation and its results are cached via cache.computeIfAbsent in get/compute, so the per-call RepositorySystem creation (which also existed before this refactor) is not a meaningful perf issue in this test-support code.

title: RabbitProperties enables SSL even when spring.rabbitmq.ssl.bundle is overridden to an empty string
message: `determineEnabled()` now uses `StringUtils.hasText(this.bundle)` for the top-level SSL config, but the PR description says the same empty-string handling should also apply to `RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl`. Could you confirm that the nested stream SSL path is updated as well, or is it intentionally handled elsewhere?
reason: The Stream class (lines 1265-1348) contains only host, port, virtualHost, username, password, and name fields—there is no nested Stream.Ssl class or bundle field, so the finding asks about handling for code that does not exist.

title: fix(http): preserve TLS options for proxy tunnels
message: The wrapper replaces `agent.callback` with a function that always merges `userHttpsAgent.options` into the callback opts. If a future `HttpsProxyAgent` version changes the callback contract or relies on instance state captured by the original method, this monkey-patch could break tunneling behavior. Consider using the agent's documented extension points (or storing a custom callback when constructing the agent) instead of mutating the instance after creation.
reason: The dependency is pinned to https-proxy-agent ^5.0.1 (package.json line 142) whose callback contract the wrapper correctly uses; the finding is an explicitly speculative "if a future version changes" maintainability nitpick rather than an actual bug.

title: fix: AxiosHeaders `toJSON()` return types
message: Could you confirm whether `toJSON()` without arguments can ever return array-valued header entries at runtime? The new signature allows `Record<string, string | string[]>` when `asStrings` is omitted, but if the default behavior always serializes to strings this broader type may weaken consumers’ type safety unnecessarily.
reason: In AxiosHeaders.toJSON (line 264), arrays are only joined when asStrings is truthy, so omitting asStrings genuinely returns array-valued entries, making the new Record<string, string | string[]> type correct rather than overly broad.

title: fix(http): preserve basic auth on same-origin redirects (#6929)
message: Comparing `new URL(redirectOptions.href).origin` to `parsed.origin` is stricter than the existing same-origin checks in Axios/follow-redirects in some edge cases. Redirects that are effectively same-origin but arrive with an equivalent hostname form (for example `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, or other URL-normalization differences) will still drop credentials, which may reintroduce 401s for valid same-origin flows. If that is intentional, could you document it; otherwise consider reusing the same-origin logic already used elsewhere in the adapter.
reason: The exact-origin comparison (lines 871-875) is the intended, correct security behavior already documented in the inline comment; treating distinct hostnames like localhost vs 127.0.0.1 as same-origin would be a security regression, not a bug, so the finding's suggestion to loosen the check is misguided.

title: Clean up error handling, fix a proto-pollution gap, and seal a few loose ends
message: `own('params')` / `own('paramsSerializer')` look like presence checks, not the actual config values. As written, `buildURL()` will no longer receive the caller-provided params or serializer, so normal query-string serialization appears broken. Please pass the property values guarded by the `own()` check instead of the check result itself.
reason: `own('params')` is defined on line 43 as a getter returning `newConfig[key]` (the actual value, or undefined), not a boolean presence check, so query-string serialization still receives the caller's params.

title: fix: guard socketPath with own() to prevent prototype pollution SSRF
message: Should inherited `socketPath` values be ignored only for security hardening, or is there any supported configuration path that still depends on prototype-derived values? This change intentionally blocks them, but it is a behavior change worth documenting for users relying on shared config objects or prototype-based defaults.
reason: The finding is an open-ended info/question (conf 0.62) about documenting an intentional security hardening, not a concrete defect; axios config is conventionally a plain object so prototype-derived socketPath is not a supported configuration path, making this a non-actionable nitpick.
